products.title: Slippery Willie's Stupid, Ugly Shoes
products.description: Review "Slippery Willie's Stupid, Ugly Shoes", by L. T. Peters---This adorable work is the first published children's book by Pinellas Park's L. T. Peters. I't's the story of Willie, a boy who doesn't walk. He slips. But then he gets some special--crazy looking--shoes. He's afraid kids at school will laugh at him for wearing the huge, red, yellow, and blue clodhoppers. And they do. And so do teachers, truck drivers, cats, dogs, birds, people in planes. Then he discovers it was all a dream. Later, when he really wears his shoes to school, no one laughs. In fact,the kids want shoes just like his." -- Book Review---Tampa Tribune, Sunday, March 9, 2008 by Karen Haymon Long, Tribune Book Editor "So many of our kids here at Gilda's Club can identify with feeling different in school and your book touched on that sensitive issue with an appropriate sense of humor---the kids LOVED it. Thank you so much." -- Amy Plain, E.C.E, B.A.A., C.L.S Noogieland Program Coordinator, Gilda's Club, Greater Toronto "What a delightful story. Best wishes." -- Gilda's Club, Delaware Valley (Warminster, PA) Cathy Kalinowski, MSS, LSW Noogieland Mgr 1)I liked it. It was funny and sweet. It is my honest opinion. I don't like comedy. Sincerely, Heaven 5)Did you write the story because you have slippery feet and stupid ugly shoes? from Brandon -- Mrs. Gaskill's 4th Grade Class,Pasadena Fundamental School, St. Petersburg, FL 1)Yes, I loved you story. It was hilarious. Why did you write it? your friend, Daniel 2)I thought this book was great and I loved it and the big shoes was hilarious. Sincerely, Star 3)I loved your book can I have some for my friends. It made me and them laugh. Love, Selena 4)Thank you very much. we all enjoyed it. Mrs. Ritchie -- Bardmoor Elementary School, Seminole, FL Mrs. Ritchie's 3rd Grade Class From the Author This is dedicated to all kids who think they are "different". It does not matter how tall or short you are, how big your nose is,how fast you can run, how high you can jump,if you can see or not, hear or not, or even be wheelchair bound, you are all God's special individual creations because God "don't make no junk". dialogue.user: Thanks for the suggestions! I’m curious about "The Spanish Game." Could you tell me a bit more about what the story is about?
dialogue.agent:
"The Spanish Game" ($17.95, 5.0 average rating, 1 review) is a suspenseful novel about Jennifer Ellis, who is drawn back into danger years after surviving an airline hijacking as a teenager. While working at the National Gallery of Art, Jennifer spots someone involved in the past incident, kicking off a new threat tied to an assassin seeking revenge for his family's death. The story follows Jennifer as she joins forces with an FBI agent and a Barcelona detective to protect her family and face deadly new threats.

Would you like to hear a customer review or more details?

result.title: The Spanish Game
result.features: Jennifer Ellis thought she had left behind the memories of the international incident where a chartered Iberian Air 727 was hijacked with she and other American high school students, including her brother.But eight years later, while working at the West Wing Gallery of the National Gallery of Art, Jennifer Ellis sees a figure involved with the incident. What was he doing in Washington, D.C.? Was he simply on vacation? If so, why did he run when he realized she'd seen him?Bent on revenge for the slaying of his family, and financed by a wealthy patron in Barcelona, Spain with his own grudge to bear, Ernesto de Rivera uses a unique and deadly high tech method of assassination. When de Rivera discovers that Henry Ellis was the one responsible for unleashing the terrorist who massacred his family he turns his attention to the Ellis family.Once again, the Ellis family is in danger. However, this time, the tables are turned. Instead of Henry Ellis trying to protect and save the lives of his children, it is his daughter, Jennifer Ellis, along with a female F.B.I. agent and a woman detective from Barcelona. Together they confront not only Ernesto de Rivera, but other heretofore unknown threats against their lives.

dialogue.user: That summary sounds interesting! I don’t need to read the customer review, but can you clarify if "The Spanish Game" stays fairly suspenseful throughout, or does it shift genres at all?
dialogue.agent:
"The Spanish Game" maintains a suspenseful and thriller-driven tone throughout the story. The plot consistently centers on danger, revenge, and high-stakes pursuit, involving international intrigue, an assassin, and law enforcement—elements that keep the narrative firmly in the suspense/thriller genre from start to finish. There are no indications that it shifts into another genre such as romance or comedy.

Would you like to proceed with this book, or are you interested in exploring more options?
